name: Bubbling Anti-de Sitter Space
description: Every smooth solution of type IIB supergravity in ten dimensions that keeps half of its supersymmetry and the symmetry of two 3-spheres, each one fixed by colouring a plane black and white. A black disc is anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions times a 5-sphere, a black half plane is the maximally supersymmetric plane wave, and any other pattern of droplets is a new geometry with no horizon. Hai Lin, Oleg Lunin, and Juan Maldacena found them in 2004, with the plane the phase space of free fermions in the dual gauge theory.
convention: The time $t$ is a pure number in every chart, so no factor of $c$ appears. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\lambda{}_{\mu\lambda\nu}$.
history: David Berenstein made a toy of Juan Maldacena's correspondence out of a single matrix in the well of a harmonic oscillator [berenstein2004, maldacena1998]. The correspondence says that string theory in anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions times a 5-sphere is the same physics as a gauge theory of four dimensions, and the toy keeps those states of the gauge theory whose energy equals their angular momentum around the sphere [maldacena1998, lin2004]. In the quantum theory the eigenvalues of the matrix are fermions, and in the ground state they fill a disc in the phase space of one eigenvalue, an "incompressible Fermi liquid droplet", since each takes up one quantum of area and no two can share it [berenstein2004, lin2004]. A graviton is a small ripple on the edge of that droplet [berenstein2004, lin2004].¶John McGreevy, Leonard Susskind, and Nicolaos Toumbas had found that a graviton with a large angular momentum around the 5-sphere blows up into a spherical brane, a giant graviton, which grows with its angular momentum until it is as large as the sphere that holds it [mcgreevy2000]. Berenstein read that brane as a hole deep in the sea of fermions, and its partner, a giant that expands inside anti-de Sitter space, as one fermion lifted far above the rest [berenstein2004]. Steve Corley, Antal Jevicki, and Sanjaye Ramgoolam had written the same states as fermions, labelled by Young diagrams, in their exact calculation of the gauge theory's correlation functions, and they had proposed the toy model before Berenstein took it up [corley2002, berenstein2004]. What geometry does a droplet of any other shape make?¶Every droplet has a spacetime of ten dimensions, and Hai Lin, Oleg Lunin, and Juan Maldacena found them all [lin2004]. Their solutions of type IIB supergravity keep half of its supersymmetry and the symmetry of two 3-spheres, and each is fixed by a single function $z$ of three coordinates that obeys the linear equation $$\partial_x^2z + \partial_w^2z + y\,\partial_y\left(\frac{\partial_yz}{y}\right) = 0$$ [lin2004]. The coordinate $y$ is the product of the radii of the two spheres, so on the plane $y = 0$ one sphere or the other shrinks to a point, and the geometry is smooth there only where $z = -1/2$ or $z = +1/2$ [lin2004]. Coloured black where $z = -1/2$ and white where $z = +1/2$, the plane is the phase space of the fermions, black where they sit [lin2004]. On a plane whose coordinates carry the dimensions of an area, a black disc of radius $L^2$ is anti-de Sitter space of radius $L$ times a 5-sphere of the same radius, and a black half plane is the plane wave that Matthias Blau, José Figueroa-O'Farrill, Christopher Hull, and George Papadopoulos found to keep all the supersymmetry of the theory [lin2004, blau2002].¶The topology of each spacetime depends only on how its droplets sit on the plane, and every pattern gives a smooth geometry with no horizon [lin2004]. A small black droplet far from the disc is a stack of branes wrapped on a 3-sphere of anti-de Sitter space, and a small white hole in the disc is a stack wrapped on a 3-sphere of the 5-sphere, the two kinds of giant graviton [lin2004]. As a droplet grows, the 3-sphere its branes wrap shrinks to a point inside it, a 5-sphere around it can no longer be shrunk to a point, and the branes are gone, replaced by the flux of the 5-form through that 5-sphere [lin2004]. That flux is the area of black inside the 5-sphere, so the black area is $2\pi\hbar$ times a whole number, with $\hbar = 2\pi l_p^4$ and $l_p$ the Planck length of ten dimensions, one cell of phase space for each fermion [lin2004].¶What does a grey disc describe? Three years before, Robert C. Myers and Øyvind Tafjord had studied supersymmetric solutions with angular momentum on the 5-sphere and a naked singularity at the centre of anti-de Sitter space, and with no horizon to hide it they called them superstars [myers2001]. They read the singularity as "a collection of giant gravitons", and those giants carry all the angular momentum of the solution [myers2001]. On the plane a superstar is a disc on which $2z$ takes the value $-1/(1 + q)$ for its charge $q$, a grey between the black of $-1$ and the white of $+1$ [lin2004]. Grey breaks the rule for smoothness, and Lin, Lunin, and Maldacena read it as fermions diluted over the disc, or a uniform gas of holes in it, which agrees with Myers and Tafjord's picture [lin2004].¶The energy of each spacetime, read from how its metric approaches anti-de Sitter space far away, is the energy of the fermions above their ground state [lin2004]. Zooming in on the border of any droplet gives back the plane wave, which is smooth, and so every border between black and white is smooth too [lin2004]. A droplet of one quantum brought closer to the disc than $\sqrt{\hbar}$ makes a spacetime curved at the Planck scale with very little energy, and since a fermion that close to the edge of the sea is one of the ripples, Lin, Lunin, and Maldacena concluded that such foam is already counted among the gravitons [lin2004]. In eleven dimensions they found the same picture for anti-de Sitter space of four and of seven dimensions, where a 2-sphere and a 5-sphere take turns shrinking on the plane, though there the function obeys the Toda equation, which they could solve only in very simple examples [lin2004].

related.text: The five large dimensions of the black disc. Every point of anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions carries a 5-sphere of the same radius, and the disc itself is the centre of anti-de Sitter space, where its 3-spheres shrink to a point [lin2004].

The throat of a stack of three-branes, anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions times a 5-sphere, is the black disc. Small droplets spread far apart on the plane become stacks of three-branes pulled apart, each with its own term in the harmonic function [lin2004, maldacena1998].

The black half plane is a plane wave of ten dimensions, $H = -\left(r_1^2 + r_2^2\right)$ across eight flat directions, which with its 5-form keeps all the supersymmetry of type IIB supergravity [blau2002, lin2004]. Zooming in on the border of any droplet gives it back [lin2004].

The same picture one dimension up. Lin, Lunin, and Maldacena found the half supersymmetric geometries of anti-de Sitter space of four dimensions times a 7-sphere as well, with a 2-sphere and a 5-sphere taking turns shrinking on a plane and a function obeying the Toda equation [lin2004].

parameters.description: Dimensionless function of $r$ and $y$; Lin, Lunin, and Maldacena's $z = \frac{1}{2}\tanh G$ obeys $\partial_r^2z + \frac{1}{r}\partial_rz + y\,\partial_y\left(\partial_yz/y\right) = 0$ and is $-1/2$ on the black rings and $+1/2$ on the white of the plane $y = 0$, which no component assumes

Dimensionless function of $r$ and $y$, the twist of the time about the axis $r = 0$, Lin, Lunin, and Maldacena's $V_\phi$; $y\,\partial_yV = r\,\partial_rz$ and $y\,\partial_rV = -r\,\partial_yz$, which no component assumes

coordinates.convention: We use Lin, Lunin, and Maldacena's coordinates $(t, r, \phi, y, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \kappa, \xi, \omega)$, with $r$ and $\phi$ polar coordinates on the plane of the droplets, $r$ and $y$ carrying the dimensions of an area, and $y$ the product of the radii of the two 3-spheres. The angles $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$ are those of the 3-sphere of radius $\sqrt{y}\,e^{G/2}$, and $\kappa$, $\xi$, and $\omega$ those of the 3-sphere of radius $\sqrt{y}\,e^{-G/2}$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

parameters.description: Radius of anti-de Sitter space and of the 5-sphere, a length; the black disc on the plane $y = 0$ has the radius $L^2$, and a clock at rest at the centre reads the proper time $Lt/c$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \rho, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \theta, \psi, \kappa, \xi, \omega)$, with $\rho$ the distance from the centre of anti-de Sitter space in units of $L$, $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$ the angles of its 3-spheres, and $\theta$, $\psi$, $\kappa$, $\xi$, and $\omega$ those of the 5-sphere. Lin, Lunin, and Maldacena's coordinates are $y = L^2\sinh\rho\sin\theta$, $r = L^2\cosh\rho\cos\theta$, and $\phi = \psi - t$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Plane Wave (the half plane)
coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, r_1, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, r_2, \kappa, \xi, \omega)$, with $x$ an area and $r_1$ and $r_2$ lengths, the radii of the two 3-spheres, whose angles are $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$ and $\kappa$, $\xi$, and $\omega$. Lin, Lunin, and Maldacena's coordinates are $y = r_1r_2$ and $w = \left(r_1^2 - r_2^2\right)/2$, with $x$ the same. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -2\,dt\,dx - \left(r_1^2 + r_2^2\right)dt^2 + dr_1^2 + r_1^2\left(d\alpha^2 + \sin^2\alpha\left(d\beta^2 + \sin^2\beta\,d\gamma^2\right)\right) + dr_2^2 + r_2^2\left(d\kappa^2 + \sin^2\kappa\left(d\xi^2 + \sin^2\xi\,d\omega^2\right)\right)
